dedupe_keys.name: availability and functionality of neonatal care units in health facilities mtwara region tanzania

description: This small facility survey records whether health facilities in the Mtwara region of southern Tanzania have working units to care for sick newborns, and whether their equipment and medicines are actually available and functioning. The producer is Serveus Kamala of the Nelson Mandela African Institution of Science and Technology. Coverage is 17 facilities, including district hospitals; 12 had at least one room for newborn care, about three quarters of newborns needing care were admitted, and there was a gap between equipment present and equipment working, for example 92 percent availability but 73 percent functioning for infant radiant warmers. The table has one row per facility and is available as a free CSV download from Dryad, mirrored on Zenodo, under the CC0 dedication. Caveats: a small regional sample, facility identities may be coded, and the qualitative findings on governance and supply are in the related article. Simulation uses: representing the gap between installed and working equipment when modelling facility capacity, and prioritising investment in neonatal units in a regional referral network. Related records: the Uganda SARA medicines data (data-uganda-sara-essential-medicines-readiness) and the WHO health infrastructure indicators (data-who-gho-health-infrastructure-indicators) cover facility readiness more widely.
name: Availability and functionality of neonatal care units in health facilities, Mtwara region, Tanzania
